column2: Add the tomato sauce and cook over low heat for 10 minutes.
Spread a little sauce in the bottom of the dish; layer lasagne sheets, meat sauce, spinach and béchamel on top.
Repeat the layers, spread béchamel on top and sprinkle with the cheese.
Cover with foil and bake for 20 minutes, then uncover and bake for 10 more minutes.
A knife should slide easily through the sheets.
Rest for 15 minutes and cut into small squares; it falls apart if cut without resting.
Wash the lettuce and chop finely; grate the carrot finely.
Warm the flatbread in a dry pan for 30 seconds to soften it.
Spread the flatbread with yoghurt; place the chicken, carrot and lettuce in the middle.
Cut in half or into 3 cm slices.
Bring the chicken to the boil with the water and skim off the foam; cook over low heat for 25 minutes.
Dice the carrot small and add to the stock; cook for 5 minutes.
Add the vermicelli and cook for 10 minutes.
Squeeze in the lemon when serving.
Add no salt or very little; daily salt should not exceed 2 g at 1–3 years and 3 g at 4–6 years.
Knead the mince and breadcrumbs; make walnut-sized flat meatballs and wash your hands.
Peel the potatoes and slice thinly; slice the tomato.
Toss the potatoes and tomatoes with olive oil and arrange on the tray; place the meatballs between them.
Bake for 30 minutes; turn the meatballs halfway.
When taking the child's portion from the family meal, set it aside before adding salt and spice.
Break the child's portion into small pieces.
Mix the drained pasta with the béchamel.
Transfer the mixture to an ovenproof dish and sprinkle with the cheese.
Boil the peas and carrot for 5 minutes and drain; mash the peas lightly.
Mix the cooked rice, vegetables, egg and cheese.
With wet hands, make walnut-sized balls and press them lightly.
Coat in breadcrumbs and arrange on the tray.
Wash the lentils and cook with 1.5 glasses of water for 15 minutes until they break down.
Turn off the heat and add the bulgur; leave covered for 20 minutes to swell.
Stir the tomato paste in the olive oil for 1 minute and add to the mixture.
Chop the spring onion and parsley very finely and add; when lukewarm, knead for 5 minutes.
Squeeze in your palm to make small patties.
Serve with lettuce leaves; chop the leaf finely.
Don't add chilli or chilli flakes.
Keep in a closed container in the fridge for 2 days.
Wash the fruit and chop into small pieces the child can chew.
Quarter grapes, cherry tomatoes and similar round foods until age 5.
Put yoghurt in the bottom of a glass; add fruit and granola on top.
Repeat the layers until the glass is full.
Add the granola just before serving; it goes soft if it stands.
Choose a low-sugar granola without nut pieces; whole nuts are a choking risk.
Cut the chicken into thin strips; break the broccoli into small florets; cut the carrot into thin sticks.
Boil the noodles in unsalted boiling water for 8–10 minutes and drain.
Heat the pan and cook the chicken for 6–7 minutes until white.
Add the vegetables and 3 spoonfuls of water; cover and soften for 5 minutes.
Soy sauce is very salty; choose a reduced-salt one and use no more than 1 teaspoon.
Cut long noodles into short pieces.
Preheat the oven to 210°C; line the tray with baking paper and grease lightly with olive oil.
Pat the whiting dry with kitchen paper; feel with your fingers and remove the bones.
Cut the fish into finger shapes the child can hold.
Put the flour, beaten egg and breadcrumbs in three separate bowls.
Coat the fish in flour, egg and breadcrumbs in turn and arrange on the tray.
Mix a little dill into yoghurt and serve as a dip on the side.
Spread the cooked quinoa in a wide dish to cool.
Peel and dice the cucumber small; chop the corn finely.
Quarter the cherry tomatoes.
Mix the quinoa and vegetables and add the olive oil.
Serve immediately; keep in the fridge for 1 day.
Knead the flour, yeast and warm water into a smooth dough.
Cover and leave in a warm place for 30 minutes.
Divide the dough into 4 and roll out small rounds together with your child.
Spread with tomato sauce; sprinkle with the cheese and finely chopped corn.
Your child can help with rolling the dough or arranging toppings; you handle the hot oven.
Bake for 12 minutes until the edges are golden and the cheese has melted.
Let cool and slice.
Add the grated tomato and cook for 5 minutes until the liquid is absorbed.
Spread the filling on the pide and sprinkle with the cheese.
Add the water; cook over low heat for 15 minutes.
Add the alphabet pasta and cook for 8 minutes until soft.
Finding letters together in the bowl makes the child more interested in eating.
Beat the egg and make a thin omelette in a buttered pan.
Fold the omelette to the size of the bread.
Put it between two slices of bread with the cheese.
Heat in a pan over medium heat for 2 minutes on each side until the cheese melts.
Cut the meat into small cubes and trim off fat and sinew.
Dice the potato, carrot, courgette and tomato.
Put all the ingredients in the clay pot with the olive oil and add 1 glass of water.
Put the clay pot into a cold oven; a sudden temperature change can crack it.
Bake at 190°C for 70 minutes until the meat is tender.
Put the clay pot on a wooden surface; it is very hot, so keep the child away.
Chop the meat small and serve with the vegetables; no pink should remain inside.
Preheat the oven to 210°C; line the tray with baking paper.
Wash and peel the sweet potato well; cut into finger-thick sticks.
Pat dry with kitchen paper; dry potatoes crisp better.
Toss with olive oil and paprika and arrange in a single, spaced-out layer on the tray.
They should be soft inside and lightly golden outside.
Add the oats, cocoa and peanut butter and mix; leave for 10 minutes.
Because of peanut allergy, if giving for the first time start with a small amount and watch.
Keep in a closed container for 3 days.
Chop the chicken small; seed the pepper and chop finely.
Add the pepper and tomato; cook covered over low heat for 10 minutes.
Serve lukewarm on a plate with cooked rice.
Lay the filo sheet on the counter; spread the filling in the middle.
Fold the edges into the middle to make a square parcel.
Melt the butter in a pan and fry the gözleme over medium heat for 3 minutes on each side.
Cool for 5 minutes and slice.
